relation_to_prior_plan.trigger: The prior plan's own feasibility gate fired: 7 of 80 transformed rulesets were rejected by the compiler with INITIAL_NO_LEGAL_MOVE, because transform A1 rotates movement atoms while leaving the generator's initial position and per-owner masks fixed. The prior plan forbade substituting a claimed transform for an unsupported one, so those 7 were recorded unsupported rather than fabricated.
relation_to_prior_plan.post_hoc_label: This follow-up was written AFTER seeing that result. It is a post-hoc follow-up, not part of the prior pre-written decision, and is reported in a separate section with that label.

question: If the whole rule geometry is rotated by one board automorphism (not only the movement atoms), is the rotated RuleSet a compiling, legality-equivalent rule, and is the served static profile still exactly equal?

transform_A3_full_rotation.square_map: sigma(f, r) = (n-1-f, n-1-r) on a square n x n board
transform_A3_full_rotation.movement_atoms: LeapAtom.offset and RayAtom.direction negated via coordinates.rotate_offset (180-degree relative rotation); max_steps unchanged
transform_A3_full_rotation.initial_position: rows reversed and row order reversed (row-major list reversed), then pieces unchanged
transform_A3_full_rotation.drop_allowed: each per-owner flat mask reversed (index i -> n*n-1-i)
transform_A3_full_rotation.promotion_allowed: every (from, to) square pair mapped through sigma
transform_A3_full_rotation.unchanged: type ids, names, anchor/promotable flags, promotion_target_ids, repetition/max_ply/stalemate policy, metadata
transform_A3_full_rotation.not_attempted: any field whose spatial meaning cannot be established from the schema is recorded unsupported rather than guessed

inputs: the same 40 deterministic seeds 292001-292040 at board sizes 6 and 8, classic_like, hand_weight 0.9; zero search, zero new seeds, zero learning
endpoint: per rule: (i) does A3 compile; (ii) one-ply legal-action bijection at the initial position - equal action count and every action maps under sigma to a legal action of the rotated rule; (iii) exact equality of normalized_board_value, normalized_hand_value, promotion_option_value and median_non_anchor_value under the identity type-id map
pre_written_decision: 80/80 compile and 80/80 one-ply bijection and 0 value mismatches => rotation_is_a_rule_isomorphism_and_profile_invariant; any compile failure => that rule unsupported with the exact error, never fabricated; any bijection failure => transform_not_a_rule_isomorphism (report the mechanism); bijection holds but a value differs => profile_not_a_function_of_rule_structure

mechanism_check.question: Does the served leaf evaluator share the profile's rotation invariance?
mechanism_check.method: for each ruleset and owner, take the evaluator's promotion zone - the set of squares with empty empty_forward_mobility - and check whether it is invariant under sigma; no evaluation of positions, no search
mechanism_check.pre_written_reading: a non-invariant zone proves the served evaluator carries an absolute-rank forward dependence that the static profile does not have; this is a structural statement only, not a strength claim

cost_estimate: under 10 min compute, well below the 120-minute assessment threshold
consumer: cross-rule static-value comparison and rule deduplication: tells whether orientation/labels can be treated as presentation detail for the profile, and separately whether the served evaluator may be treated the same way
nonduplication_check: not the PRIMARY ray->leap re-encoding test, not PRIMARY 411001-411008, not AUX92/93, not the closed hand-policy fixture, no frozen fitness
limitations: one generator family (classic_like), square boards 6 and 8, 40 seeds; the one-ply bijection is a bounded legality check and is not a claim of full game-tree equivalence; rotation invariance is undefined on rectangular boards here; no strength, utility or outcome claim
